Subject: Operational data paths & pinning — follow-up and next steps

Hi Lina / James —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

1) What we heard (confirm if I missed anything)
   - HealthBridge needs PII and patient identifiers for the US region to remain within US-only compute and persistent storage.
   - System logs (API request/response samples) can be routed to a central observability plane in the US, but you want tighter controls on full request bodies.
   - For disaster recovery you expect cross-region failover only to another US region (no EU or APAC fallback) unless explicitly consented per dataset.

2) Clarifying questions for you (so we can size the proposal):
   - Can you confirm if redaction at client-side (before sending) is acceptable for non-essential PII, or do you need in-flight redaction at our edge?
   - RPO target for persistent model state / embeddings: is 4h acceptable, or do you require sub-1h restores for critical workloads?
   - How long do you need request/response logs retained for audit? (e.g., 30 / 90 / 365 days)

3) Proposed short-term plan (what Redwood can deliver quickly)
   - Provide a US-only pin for production workloads (compute + persistent storage) and a warm-standby in a secondary US region.
   - Ship a minimal Evidence Pack (SOC2 excerpts + configuration screenshots) and a one-page data flow diagram. Attached: redwood-region-pinning-diagram.png and initial healthbridge-data-matrix.xlsx (stub).

4) Next steps / owners
   - Lina: confirm retention window and redaction tolerance.
   - HealthBridge privacy: share any specific contractual language required for location-binding.
   - Monica (CCed): we’ll need a short checklist of evidence to attach to the AR contract.
   - Proposed follow-up: Wed 10/29 10:00am PT for an ops-level technical sync.

If that matches your understanding, Lina, we’ll prepare a short scoped doc and a Dedicated/Private options comparison.

Thanks —

Ben

Subject: Re: Operational data paths & pinning — follow-up and next steps

Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from our privacy team (copied):

> On redaction: client-side redaction is preferred for high-risk fields (SSN, MRN), but we do need full request content available to the vendor for debugging on a case-by-case basis under a documented process (access review + narrow time window).

> RPO: critical production embeddings and model state must be recoverable within 1 hour for our triage flows. Non-critical analytic workloads can accept a 6–12h RPO.

> Logs: we need request/response logs retained for 365 days for compliance, but access controls should ensure only approved auditors can retrieve full payloads.

Also: on failover — we must not have automatic failover to EU/APAC for any workload marked as country-locked. Manual DR playbooks to move to another US region are acceptable.

We’re comfortable with the proposed follow-up time (10/29) — can you add a brief agenda? Also attach any sample access-review checklist you normally use.

Thanks,
Lina
Lina Park
Head of Platform Compliance, HealthBridge
lina.park@healthbridge.io

Monica / Laura — quick internal sync notes from Lina’s reply:

- They require 1h RPO for critical state (embeddings/model state) — we should plan a Dedicated+snapshot cadence or offer managed incremental backups with 30–60m checkpoints.
- 365d log retention for request/response payloads but with gated access. Need to confirm if we can provide field-level encryption for stored logs or if redaction plus access controls is the preferred route.
- Failover: no EU/APAC automatic fallbacks for country-locked datasets; manual DR only.

Action items: 
- Monica: can you pull the SOC2 evidence extract we used for the Acme/HIT integration and redline the pieces around log retention/access? I attached a draft extract (redwood-soc2-evidence-extract.pdf).
- Laura: please draft a one-page agenda for 10/29 ops sync: 1) retention + access model, 2) RPO options + design, 3) evidence checklist and timelines.
- I’ll prepare a short technical appendix that describes pinning options (primary US region + warm standby in secondary US region) and the proposed snapshot frequency.

If either of you sees a blocker (policy or infra), flag it and I’ll loop Markus. We want to have a scoped plan to share by EOD Mon 10/27.

Thanks —
Ben

- Engineering: Ben, ask the infra team to validate 30–60m checkpoint feasibility for embeddings. If 30m checkpoints add >20% cost, present a 60m baseline with an optional premium.

I’m OK to be on the 10/29 call for the first 15 minutes to speed approvals. Laura, coordinate a calendar invite and include the Drive link to the proposed configuration doc.
